content.intro: In this lesson, you will study introduction to functional programming in java with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you represent small units of behavior clearly without hiding state changes in callbacks. In this lesson, focus on functions as values through functional interfaces and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

items.title: Declarative versus imperative code
items.text: Compare the alternatives in declarative versus imperative code by their contract, trade-offs, failure modes, and fit for the current requirement; do not choose by familiarity alone.

items.title: Transforming and filtering data
items.text: Lambdas supply behavior for functional interfaces, while method references reuse existing methods. Keep callbacks small, predictable, and free of unnecessary shared-state mutation. Apply that reasoning specifically to transforming and filtering data and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

items.title: Side effects and immutability
items.text: Make responsibilities and contracts explicit. Prefer small cohesive types, stable interfaces, testable dependencies, and immutable value objects where they reduce accidental state changes.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
